pr.title: perf(context): add fast path to c.json() matching c.text() optimization

summary: This PR adds a fast path to c.json() mirroring the existing c.text() optimization, using Response.json(object) when no status/headers/finalized state exists. The new fast path relies on the platform's built-in Response.json() implementation instead of the previous manual JSON.stringify + setDefaultContentType flow, which could subtly differ in content-type formatting or error behavior (e.g., BigInt/circular references) compared to the slow path. The existing tests only exercise the slow path (with status/headers args), so the new bare c.json({...}) fast path isn't directly verified for header/content-type parity or correct output.

findings.rationale: The fast path uses `Response.json(object)` (built-in Web API) instead of manually constructing `new Response(JSON.stringify(object), { headers: {...} })` as done previously. Response.json() re-serializes via its own JSON.stringify equivalent and sets Content-Type per spec; if `object` contains values that throw during stringification (e.g., BigInt, circular refs) the error path/type could differ subtly from the previous `#newResponse` path, and there's no test asserting the exact header value/casing/charset match between fast and slow paths for c.json().
findings.suggestedCheck: Add/verify a test that calls c.json({...}) with no status/headers and asserts res.headers.get('Content-Type') exactly equals 'application/json' (not e.g. 'application/json; charset=UTF-8') to ensure parity with the previous behavior.

findings.rationale: No new test was added specifically for the new json() fast path (i.e., c.json(obj) called with zero additional arguments and no prior header/status/finalized state) even though the c.text() fast path presumably has coverage; existing c.json() test only covers the arg+headers case which forces the slow path.
findings.suggestedCheck: Confirm test suite includes a case for bare `c.json({...})` with no arg/headers to lock in the new fast-path output shape.
